title: Validate marketplace webhooks and add audit logging for provisioning events
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Marketplace purchase → provisioning depends on inbound provider events (AWS/GCP) to activate entitlements and link to Redwood orgs. We need stronger validation of inbound events plus a durable audit trail of what we received/processed to satisfy marketplace security review requirements and to speed up support investigations.

This ticket covers:
- Webhook/event validation (authenticity + integrity) for AWS + GCP marketplace provisioning events.
- Audit logging: record each inbound event with verification status, processing outcome, and pointers needed for later forensics (without storing sensitive payloads).
- Documented security review checklist and sign-off requirements (SecEng/GRC) before rollout.
acceptance_criteria:
- All inbound marketplace provisioning events are validated before processing:
  - AWS: validate SNS signature + certificate chain per AWS guidance; reject unsigned/invalid messages; enforce allowlist on TopicArn(s).
  - GCP: validate Google-signed OIDC/JWT token for Pub/Sub push (issuer, audience, exp); reject missing/invalid tokens.
  - Enforce request size limits; reject unsupported content-types; hard-fail on invalid JSON.
  - Maintain idempotency: dedupe based on provider message id (AWS MessageId / GCP messageId) and event type.

- Audit trail exists for every received event (including rejected events) with:
  - provider (aws|gcp), provider_event_id, received_at, verification_result, rejection_reason (if any)
  - processing_status (received|validated|rejected|processed|failed), processed_at
  - mapped internal identifiers (redwood_org_id if known, entitlement_id, sku_id) where applicable
  - correlation identifiers (request_id/trace_id) for linking to service logs and support tickets

- Audit logs do NOT store raw request bodies or secrets. Payload stored as a one-way hash (sha256) and minimal safe fields needed for debugging.

- Audit records are queryable by Support/SRE via internal admin tooling / SQL runbook with documented examples.

- Monitoring added:
  - Counter for invalid signature/JWT failures by provider
  - Counter for webhook processing failures
  - SLI/SLO-friendly metric for event processing latency (received → processed)

- Security review completed and documented:
  - Threat model notes included in this ticket
  - Marcus Lin (SecEng) approves validation approach and logging/redaction
  - Olga Petrov (GRC) confirms audit log retention/access posture is consistent with marketplace security packet language

- Rollout is behind a feature flag with a clear backout plan (can revert to prior validation behavior without downtime).
implementation_notes:
Proposed approach
1) Validation layer (pre-handler middleware)
- Common: enforce max body size (e.g., 256KB), validate Content-Type, parse JSON with strict mode, attach a deterministic "event_fingerprint" (sha256 over normalized minimal fields).
- AWS SNS:
  - Parse SNS envelope (Type/MessageId/TopicArn/Timestamp/Signature/SigningCertURL).
  - Validate SigningCertURL host is an AWS SNS domain.
  - Fetch and cache the signing certificate with bounded TTL.
  - Verify signature per AWS SNS spec.
  - Enforce TopicArn allowlist (env-configured) to prevent cross-topic spoofing.
- GCP Pub/Sub push:
  - Validate Authorization Bearer token is present.
  - Verify JWT signature using Google certs; verify iss/aud/exp.
  - Extract Pub/Sub messageId and publishTime.

2) Audit logging
- Create durable storage for audit events (table or append-only log index). Fields:
  - id (uuid), provider, provider_event_id, event_type, received_at
  - verification_status (passed|failed), verification_details (short code)
  - processing_status + error_code
  - redwood_org_id (nullable), entitlement_id (nullable), sku_id (nullable)
  - payload_hash (sha256), safe_metadata (selected non-sensitive fields)
  - request_id / trace_id
- Add a structured log line for each stage; keep payload out of logs.

3) Access controls & retention
- Limit read access to audit table to oncall/SRE/support via existing break-glass group.
- Default retention aligned to current control-plane audit retention (confirm with GRC); do not claim customer-configurable retention unless productized as an add-on.

4) Error handling
- On validation failure: return 401/403 (auth) or 400 (format) and write audit record with rejection reason.
- On processing failure: 5xx with retryable semantics where provider supports retries; write audit record with failed status and error code.

Open questions
- Finalize exact provider integration details for GCP push (OIDC audience string) to match our production endpoint URL.
- Confirm whether AWS path is direct HTTP SNS delivery vs SQS subscription; if SQS, validation moves to message consumer (still validate signature fields).
testing_plan:
Automated
- Unit tests for AWS SNS signature validation (valid, invalid signature, invalid cert URL, wrong topic, replayed MessageId)
- Unit tests for GCP JWT validation (valid token, wrong aud, expired, wrong issuer, missing token)
- Unit tests for audit log redaction (ensure raw payload never persisted)
- Integration tests using provider fixtures to ensure idempotency + dedupe behavior

Manual / staging
- Simulate provider events in staging; verify:
  - accepted events process successfully and create audit records
  - rejected events do not create entitlements and still create audit records
  - metrics increment correctly and dashboards show expected signals
- Support runbook validation: query by provider_event_id and trace_id to locate event history end-to-end.
rollout_plan:
1) Land behind feature flag: marketplace.webhook_validation_v2
2) Enable in staging for AWS only, then GCP
3) Enable in prod for 5% of traffic (or subset of topics/subscriptions) for 24h; monitor validation failures + processing latency
4) Ramp to 100% after 48h with stable metrics
Backout: disable flag to revert to previous behavior (processing continues but without strict validation). If audit storage causes issues, keep structured logs only as temporary fallback (with payload redaction enforced).
comments: 2025-02-10 — Talia Benson: Creating separate ticket for validation + audit logging so it’s explicitly covered in the security packet review. This is a must-have for AWS/GCP review cycles and for support forensics when entitlements lag.

2025-02-12 — Ethan Park: Plan is middleware validation + an append-only audit table keyed by provider_event_id. Will coordinate with Marcus on redaction requirements. Also adding a hard body-size limit; we’ve seen noisy payloads during partner testing.

2025-02-14 — Marcus Lin: Please do NOT store raw webhook payloads in DB or logs. Hash is fine; additionally, store only minimal safe fields (event type, sku id, entitlement id, timestamps). Make sure signature/JWT verification failures are tracked as metrics (we’ll want to prove this control exists).

2025-02-18 — Rafael Mendes: +1 on metrics. Recommend: webhook_invalid_auth_total{provider,reason}, webhook_processing_failed_total{provider,stage}, and a histogram for processing_latency_seconds. Also ensure the audit event includes trace_id so we can jump into tracing.

2025-02-21 — Ethan Park: Implemented audit persistence + validation hooks, wired into the ingestion service. PRs in flight: AWS path has SNS signature verification; GCP path has JWT verification w/ aud allowlist. Added dedupe on provider_event_id. Still need final confirmation of GCP audience string from Partnerships.

2025-02-26 — Olga Petrov: Reviewed proposed audit fields. OK as long as access is restricted and we don’t claim configurable retention in the security packet. Please add a note in the security packet draft that audit logs are available for provisioning events and are access-controlled.

2025-03-01 — Ethan Park: Staging validated. Found one edge case: AWS SNS sends SubscriptionConfirmation. We now explicitly handle/ack those without attempting entitlement processing, but still audit-log receipt. Marking ready for final SecEng review + flag-controlled prod canary.
2025-03-03 — Connor O'Brien: For release notes: include "marketplace event validation + audit logging" under control-plane-2025.03. Please confirm backout is just flag disable (no schema rollback).
2025-03-03 — Ethan Park: Confirmed. Backout is flag disable; schema stays. If needed we can stop writes to audit table via config, but we should keep it on for forensics.
